Hi Hanna,

Great question! You can archive your finished project in just a few clicks, and yes, you can bring it back anytime if needed.

To archive the project:
1. Go to Projects and open the project you want to archive.
2. Click Settings > Archive project.
3. Confirm the action in the dialog.
4. The project will disappear from your active project list and move to Projects > Archived.

Once archived, the project becomes read-only (no one can create, edit, or delete tasks), but you can still view it and all its tasks. Since you're an Admin, you have the permissions needed to do this.

If you need to bring it back later, just go to Projects > Archived, find the project, click the three-dot menu next to its name, and select Restore. The project will return to your active list with everything intact.

Archiving won't delete any data, and archived projects don't count toward your plan limits, so this should help with the performance issue you mentioned with the large task list.

Let us know if you have any other questions!

Quillstack Support

Hi Hugo,

Great question—two-factor authentication is a smart way to secure your account. Here are the steps to enable it with your authenticator app:

1. Sign in to Quillstack at app.quillstack.com and click your avatar in the top right corner.
2. Select Account settings from the dropdown menu.
3. Go to the Security tab.
4. Click Enable two-factor authentication.
5. Open your authenticator app and scan the QR code displayed on the screen. If you cannot scan the code, click Enter key manually and type the text key into your app.
6. Your authenticator app will display a six-digit code that refreshes every 30 seconds. Enter the current code in the Verification code field and click Verify and enable.
7. Quillstack will display 10 recovery codes. Copy these codes and store them in a safe place, such as a password manager or a secure note. Each code can be used only once.
8. Check the box confirming you have saved your recovery codes, then click Done.

After setup, you'll need both your password and a code from your authenticator app every time you sign in. Your web sessions expire after 30 days of inactivity, and mobile app sessions expire after 90 days, so you'll be prompted for a new code when your session ends.

Make sure to save those recovery codes somewhere secure—they're your backup if you ever lose access to your authenticator device.

Quillstack Support

Hi Tomas,

Great question! Quillstack lets you organize pages into a folder structure to create the hierarchy you're looking for.

Here's how to organize your documentation:

1. In the sidebar, click the **···** menu next to a page and select **Move to folder**.
2. Choose an existing folder from the list or click **New folder** to create one.
3. Enter a folder name and click **Create**. The page moves into the folder and the sidebar updates.

You can also drag and drop pages directly onto folders in the sidebar. If you want to create nested folders (folders within folders), just drag one folder onto another. You can nest folders up to 5 levels deep, which should give you plenty of room to organize your documentation structure.

Let me know if you run into any issues!

Quillstack Support

records.draft:
Hi Ivan,

Thank you for reaching out. I understand your accounting team would prefer invoices in EUR now that your office is in Frankfurt.

Unfortunately, the billing currency for a workspace cannot be changed after it's created. The currency is set permanently when you first set up your workspace and applies to all future invoices and charges.

If you need to switch to EUR billing, the only option is to export your workspace content from Settings > Data > Export, create a new workspace with EUR as the billing currency, and import the exported data into it. Workspace exports can take up to 24 hours and the download link is valid for 7 days. Your old workspace can then be deleted if you no longer need it.

Quillstack Support
